notes.WRSPM: 2s: designated phenomena (domain entities), W as indicative domain knowledge, and shared phenomena e_v/s_v at the environment-machine interface. 1s: environment/machine only as controllers of phenomena (actor), optative R (goal), the environment as a whole (context), events/actions as kinds of phenomena, and Zave & Jackson's discussion of timing and no anticipation of future events.
notes.Problem Frames: 2s: domains typed as biddable or causal (actor), given/lexical domains and phenomena (domain entity), indicative domain descriptions, the context diagram, interfaces of shared phenomena, and event as a defined phenomenon class. 1s: requirement oval (goal), constraining references (constraint), the reliability and overrun concerns (uncertainty, time), domain-controlled events (action), and state-machine domain descriptions (process).
notes.KAOS: 2s: Agent, Goal, Objects (entity/relationship/event), domain invariants and hypotheses, Constraint/requirement, real-time temporal logic operators, Obstacle, and Operation. 1s: goal categories such as safety, accuracy and security (quality), current-condition goal patterns (context), monitor/control links (interaction), operation input/output objects (resource), pre/post/trigger conditions (process), and refinement links as rationale (provenance).
notes.iStar: 2s: Actor/Role/Agent, Goal, Softgoal/Quality, Dependency, Task and Resource. 1s: actors also stand in for stakeholders, Resource doubles as the only domain-entity notion, and the Strategic Rationale model gives means-end rationale.
notes.CORE: 2s: functional goal and softgoal, quality constraint and softgoal (quality), domain assumption (domain property), and plan (action). 1s: stakeholders appear only as the speakers of communicated information, and the quality constraint is the only kind of constraint.
notes.Dey: 2s: entity (person, place or object), context as the information that characterises an entity's situation, and time and location as primary context types. 1s: users/persons as an entity category (actor), context information as entity attributes (domain property), user-application interaction, activity as a context type (action), and context changes that trigger services (event).
notes.Contextual goal models: 2s: Tropos actors, goals, softgoals, dependencies and plans, context annotations at variation points, and facts as verifiable world predicates (domain property). 1s: actors double as stakeholders, a class diagram of data for verifying facts (domain entity), contexts restricting applicable alternatives (constraint), non-verifiable statements (uncertainty), and inherited Tropos resources.
notes.Uncertainty taxonomy: 2s: uncertainty itself, through its definition, sources and classification by phase. 1s: falsifiable assumptions as a source (domain property), and the template's context field plus unpredictable environment as a source (context).
notes.RELAX: 2s: ENV environmental properties (domain property), temporal operators EVENTUALLY/UNTIL/BEFORE/AFTER/IN, and uncertainty factors with relaxation operators. 1s: requirements as optative statements (goal), entities referenced by ENV, invariant SHALL requirements (constraint), ENV as operating conditions (context), MON/REL (interaction), events as operands of BEFORE/AFTER, and DEP dependencies between requirements (provenance).
notes.ISO 29148: 2s: defined terms for stakeholder (and the StRS) and constraint (including design constraints), plus traceability with requirement attributes such as source and rationale. 1s: information items such as users, business objectives, quality/performance requirement types, logical data, assumptions and dependencies, OpsCon/ConOps, the risk/stability attributes, interface requirements, functions, and business processes/scenarios.
notes.SysML v2: Coded at the language level that requirement definitions and usages reference. 2s: actor and stakeholder parameters, part/item definitions, attributes and assume constraints, constraint definitions, time slices/snapshots and time triggers, interfaces/connections/flows, actions, successions and state machines, event occurrences and accept triggers, and satisfy/verify/derivation with Rationale metadata. 1s: concerns/objectives (goal), quality only as attribute constraints, subject and system context (context), the SpatialItems library (location), and items consumed by actions (resource).
notes.Traceability reference model: 2s: Stakeholder in the meta-model, constraints (standards, policies, methods), and trace links plus rationale (provenance). 1s: stakeholders who act on objects (actor), organisational/strategic needs (goal), assumptions in the rationale sub-model (domain property), and timestamps under the 'when' dimension (time).
